title.en: Stacks and queues in Java: circular queue and deque

hook.en: Plates are taken from the top of a pile (stack); tickets are given to the front of a line (queue). Java programs build both with an array and a couple of index variables.

objectives.en: Implement a stack with an array: push, pop, peek, overflow and underflow
Implement a linear and a circular queue with front and rear
Describe a deque and its operations

narration.en: Plates are taken from the top of a pile (stack); tickets are given to the front of a line (queue). Java programs build both with an array and a couple of index variables.

body.en: A stack is a LIFO (last in, first out) structure. With an array arr of size cap and an index top (−1 when empty): push(x) checks for overflow (top == cap − 1), then arr[++top] = x; pop() checks for underflow (top == −1), then returns arr[top−−]; peek() returns arr[top] without removing it. Stacks are used for undo, the call stack, reversing and evaluating postfix expressions.

body.en: A queue is FIFO (first in, first out): elements are added at the rear and removed from the front. In a linear array queue, front and rear only move right, so space is wasted; a circular queue reuses cells with % cap. A deque (double-ended queue) allows insertion and deletion at both ends: addFront, addRear, deleteFront, deleteRear. An input-restricted deque allows insertion at one end only; an output-restricted deque allows deletion at one end only. A deque can act as both a stack and a queue.

body.en: In a circular queue, every index that moves forward is written (i + 1) % cap. When i is the last cell, the % brings it back to 0.
